description:
A Asa Branca Aerospace é uma equipe universitária de foguetemodelismo da UFCG, em Campina Grande (PB). Reunimos estudantes de diferentes cursos para projetar, simular, construir e lançar foguetes, com foco em propulsão química, segurança e inovação. Construimos foguetes, desenvolvemos conhecimento e mais que inovação também nascente no Nordeste.

Instagram: asabranca.ufcg

E-mail: asabranca.aerospace@eq.ufcg.edu.br
summary:
Due to the lack of in-depth and organized studies on how combustion works in microgravity, there is an enormous amount of spread information, of difficult interpretation and use. In this case, the access to science-based data is hindered, generating an unneeded amount of stress on the researcher. 
The Firefly Project emerges as a web dashboard that brings together the research-obtained statistics directly from NASA’s database on how flames behave in microgravity, using a great range of variables, such as temperature, pressure, material type and others to train a Super Intelligence (SI) local model. The aim is to identify, collect and organize the best set of data that are coherent to the user’s query, avoiding redundant information and SI hallucinations. 
As the final goal, it is targeted to obtain an efficient and compelling system, enhancing the user’s experience through  allowing it to filter, among an immense amount of studies, the information needed. Lastly, the system returns a graphic with all the structured data and its respective references, assisting the research and giving insights on troubleshooting.
details:
The Firefly project is a web dashboard that uses a Super Intelligence (SI) to organize data from NASA on the behavior of combustion and flames in microgravity, including their interactions under different conditions of temperature, pressure, oxidizers, and other factors, helping the user make more assertive decisions without being overwhelmed by infinite, nonsensical tables.

This help, as a database-based search tool, provides the veracity of the information shown and makes it possible to check the sources of the results. As an AI-powered platform that provides insights, the database is constantly updated, giving users the freedom to analyze archives they think are relevant.

As a database-based search tool, the assistance ensures the accuracy of the information shown, and it is even possible to check the sources of each result. As an AI-powered platform that displays insights, the database is constantly updated during use, giving users the freedom to analyze any files they find relevant. Results are then presented in a concise and filterable way to ensure the best user experience. Firefly also includes an LLM in its workspace that can answer users’ direct questions about the topic, with answers grounded in the database that feeds the dashboard.

The main impact we want Firefly to have is a major gain in efficiency for researchers, made possible by the systematic organization and quick recall of experimental data from previous research on the topic. This spares scientists the unnecessary stress of exhaustive searches to understand how flames behave in microgravity and how they respond to specific conditions.

Firefly’s core development, including data analysis and coding, was done through vibe coding, and an SI system then handled the data processing. The tools used to build the system were Python, ChromaDB, RAG, Streamlit, Pandas, PyMuPDF, SQLite, an embeddings model, a local LLM, Ollama, Plotly, Pint, Git/Github, NumPy, Pillow, Torch, Sentence-Transformers, Transformers, Tokenizers, Hugging Face Hub, and OpenPyXL. We used Krita to draw the logo and build a visual identity that accurately represents the platform. All of these tools were essential to structuring the system, hosting the SI, and making Firefly work effectively.

It is worth highlighting the innovations in our interface. An O₂ (Oxygen) and pressure calculator helps simulate the microgravity conditions a flame would experience aboard space stations and in other environments. The platform also includes a gap matrix, which organizes the data and makes it easier to identify which evidence is available in the database.

A key part of our creative process was building our own visual identity, with a hand-drawn logo that follows the colors and the woodcut (xilogravura) aesthetic, a traditional art form from Northeast Brazil, in the design of our team, Asa Branca Aerospace.

In designing the dashboard, our team considered the everyday experience of scientists and researchers, who spend much of their working lives searching for information and trying to organize it for their projects. Firefly was created to speed up this process, saving time and reducing waste. Its application is not limited to burning materials in microgravity: thanks to its updatable, adaptable database, the system can be reused for other processes and research involving massive amounts of data.

Firefly was created to solve NASA’s challenge. Still, it is also a highly applicable product that can solve the same problem for scientists in other fields, making it commercially viable and dynamic.
